newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-GERMANS POISED TO RETAIN EUROPEAN CUPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GERMANS POISED TO RETAIN EUROPEAN CUPS.

text.p: Germany look set to maintain their domination of European athletics before their home fans at the weekend.
The Germans are favoured to retain both their men's and women's European Cup titles after two days of competition on Saturday and Sunday in Munich.
German men's teams have won the Cup on the last three occasions and last year had a 17 points margin over Britain.

Among the leading names in their squad are Olympic discus champion Lars Riedal, who has already set a personal best this year, and Dieter Baumann, the 1992 Olympic 5,000 metres gold medallist, who runs over 3,000 metres.
Britain have finished in second place five times since they last won the title in 1989.
Former Olympic champion Linford Christie will be the British men's captain for the last time. The 37-year-old veteran is aiming for a record eighth successive 100 metres victory in the European Cup.

Olympic silver medallists triple jumper Jonathan Edwards and javelin thrower Steve Backley, both of whom have shown impressive early season form, will ensure that the men's contest is not dominated solely by the Germans.
The pole vault could be one of the most enthralling individual competitions with France's Jean Galfione, the Olympic champion, up against his predecessor, Maxim Tarasov of Russia.
Norway and Greece were both promoted to the Super League last year but will be struggling all weekend to retain their status.
Norway, at least, can rely on Olympic 800 metres champion Verbjorn Rodal, who underlined his form with a win in the Helsinki Grand Prix meeting on Wednesday.
In the women's events, the main protagonists are expected to be Germany and Russia, who have won the last five titles between them.
Russia will expect maximum points from triple jumper Inna Lasovskaya and discus thrower Natalya Sadova.
Both took silver medals in Atlanta and the athletes who finished in front of them are missing in Munich.
Ukraine have named Yelena Govorova in the triple jump rather than Inessa Kravets while Germany preferred Franka Dietzsch to Ilke Wyludda for the discus event.
Germany, led by Olympic shot put champion Astrid Kumbernuss, appear slightly stronger overall than their Russian rivals.
The other nations are expected to be well adrift of the two principal contenders but do hope to shine in some events.

France will count on Marie-Jose Perec, favoured to win the 200 metres -- one of the two races in which she won gold at last year's Olympics -- while Romania will look for a win by Gabriela Szabo, the world indoor 3,000 metres champion, who chose to enter the 1,500 metres.
